task.title: Set up the Linux source checkout
task.shortdesc: Clone the BPM repository, create the Python virtual environment, install development dependencies, and prepare the local database schema.

prereq.p: The Linux host is prepared, and the administrator has access to the BPM repository URL and the approved target branch, tag, or revision.

context.p: The repository README defines the supported source setup sequence. Use repository-local commands so later troubleshooting can compare the environment with committed scripts.

step.cmd: Clone the repository and enter the checkout.

info.codeblock: git clone <repository-url> browser-policy-manager cd browser-policy-manager git checkout <approved-0.9.1-ref>
info.p: Replace placeholders with the approved internal repository URL and release reference.

step.cmd: Create and activate the local Python environment.

info.codeblock: python -m venv .venv source .venv/bin/activate python -m pip install --upgrade pip
info.p: The virtual environment stays inside the checkout and is not committed.

step.cmd: Install BPM source dependencies from the checkout.

info.p: The editable install keeps runtime code and tests aligned with the current source tree.

step.cmd: Apply database migrations for the selected runtime database.

info.note: Run migrations only against the intended BPM database. For the default source workflow this is the local SQLite database, not a production service database.

result.p: The checkout has an activated Python environment, installed dependencies, and a migrated database schema.

postreq.p: Configure the runtime environment before starting the application process.
